clue.text: Angry allusion requiring concordance?

definitions.note: a phrase standing for the noun: the kind of note a concordance or index calls for

parts.note: angry means cross
an allusion is a reference to something

explanation.surface: Someone makes a bitter allusion that seems to demand agreement from others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concordance' suggests agreement, but here it is a reference index, which points the reader elsewhere with notes like 'see also'.
explanation.definitionFit: A concordance is an alphabetical index of words, and such indexes rely on pointers directing the reader to related entries.

clue.text: Reserve has to teach during break

indicators.note: during says one word sits in the middle of another, here the teaching inside the break

parts.note: a break is a rest
to teach is to train

explanation.surface: A teacher must hold back their feelings while on a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserve' looks like a store kept back, but it means self-control; 'during' signals that the teaching word goes inside the word for a break.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserve and restraint are both synonyms for holding oneself back.

clue.text: Greek wood-god or stray hybrid

indicators.note: a hybrid is a mixture, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A wood-god of Greek myth is compared to a mongrel stray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hybrid' tells you to mix up the letters of STRAY.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek mythology satyrs are woodland deities, half man and half goat.

clue.text: Twice prepared but not bespoken

parts.note: prepared means ready
prepared also means made, as a bed is made

explanation.surface: Something got ready twice over still isn't made to measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twice' asks for two different words for 'prepared'. 'Bespoken' plays on bespoke, meaning made to order.
explanation.definitionFit: Bespoke clothing is tailored to order, while off-the-peg items are manufactured in advance for anyone.

clue.text: Cast and force fish to follow

indicators.note: to follow says the fish comes after the force

parts.note: F is the physics abbreviation for force
a ling is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: An angler casts, using some force, so a fish will follow the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like fishing talk, but it is the definition, meaning to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast something is to throw it, which is a synonym.

clue.text: Arguing about a child, in Gateshead

parts.note: re is Latin-derived for about, concerning
a son is a child
the head of Gates, its first letter; Gateshead is also a town in north-east England

explanation.surface: A family in Gateshead is quarrelling about one of the children.
explanation.walkthrough: Gateshead, a town in north-east England, splits as Gates + head, giving the first letter of Gates.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasoning means making a case or debating a point logically, so it is a synonym.

clue.text: Din created by hooter about one

indicators.note: about says one piece goes around another, the hooter wrapping the one

parts.note: hooter is slang for the nose
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A loud racket made by a car horn going around once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hooter' suggests a horn making a din, but it is British slang for a nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Din and racket are both synonyms for loud sound.

clue.text: Reserved fruit in the end

indicators.note: in says the fruit is placed inside the word for the end

parts.note: end as written, the finish
a gage is a kind of plum, as in greengage

explanation.surface: Fruit set aside for later is finally eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals that the fruit goes inside; read on the surface, 'in the end' looks like a phrase meaning finally.
explanation.definitionFit: A table or phone line that is booked or occupied is engaged, a synonym for reserved.

clue.text: Drink for each meal

parts.note: to sup is to drink
per means for each, as in per person

explanation.surface: A drink for every person at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: An evening meal, eaten late in the day, is a synonym.

clue.text: Disturb the elite

definitions.meaning: to disturb is to unsettle someone
the top group or set, read as a set that is up

explanation.definitionFit: Upset means unsettle; read as two words, 'up set' is the topmost social group, the elite.

clue.text: Enlivening or taming in a jungle

indicators.note: a jungle is a tangled mess, so these letters are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A lion tamer brings the act to life in a jungle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jungle' reads as a place but signals rearranging TAMING IN A.
explanation.definitionFit: Enlivening and bringing to life are synonyms.

clue.text: Draw wine and beam

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: Someone pours wine and smiles broadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' sounds like pouring a drink, and 'beam' like a smile; here they mean depict and a shaft of light.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a subject is to depict it, a synonym.

clue.text: Exclamation of approval heard in the hen-house?

definitions.meaning: a dated British cry of praise, like well done
read literally, a fine egg is what a hen produces in the coop

explanation.definitionFit: The old British phrase praises a reliable person; literally it describes a sound product of a laying hen.

clue.text: Feeling remorse for bankrupt with only one note

parts.note: to bankrupt someone is to ruin them
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: A ruined businessman regrets being left with a single banknote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' suggests a banknote after bankruptcy, but it is a musical note, one of A to G.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel remorse for something is to regret it, a synonym.

clue.text: Poetic jewellery manufacturer?

parts.note: a craftsman working precious metal who also shares a surname with an 18th-century Irish poet and playwright

explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Goldsmith wrote poetry, and the trade name means a worker who makes items in a precious yellow metal.

clue.text: A group of detectives I fired without right turned sour

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

indicators.note: without says a letter is taken away from the word fired

explanation.surface: A detective team member who was sacked became bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes R out of FIRED to leave FIED. CID is the detective branch of a UK police force.
explanation.definitionFit: To acidify is to make something acidic, and acidic tastes are sour.

clue.text: Meddle and engrave iron with soldiers

parts.note: to engrave read as en-grave, put in a grave, means to inter or bury
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Someone tampers by etching an iron object with toy soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engrave' is read as en-grave, to place in a grave, which is to bury.
explanation.definitionFit: To meddle and to interfere both mean to involve yourself unwanted in others' affairs.

clue.text: Signora must lose the way to become a fool

indicators.note: lose says letters are taken away from the words Signora must

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: An Italian lady must give up her path or end up foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing S from the front and T from the end of SIGNORAMUST leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An ignorant person lacking knowledge is a dunce, a synonym for fool.

clue.text: Mind being at home to relate badly etc.

parts.note: in means at home
to relate a story is to tell it

indicators.note: badly says the letters of etc are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A mind at home tells stories poorly, trailing off with etc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' scrambles only ETC to ECT; 'relate' is TELL, not anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Mind and intellect are synonyms for the power of thought.

clue.text: Arraign the devil before everyone

indicators.note: before says the devil piece comes first

parts.note: an imp is a little devil
each means every one

explanation.surface: Charge the devil in front of all.
explanation.definitionFit: To arraign is to call someone before a court to face charges, which is a synonym.

clue.text: Beyond hope of recovery? Dead right!

definitions.note: an adjective phrase for a noun: someone beyond hope

parts.note: dead means gone

explanation.surface: A doctor declares a patient past saving: totally dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead right' looks like 'absolutely correct', but it splits into dead and right.
explanation.definitionFit: A person past saving is described informally as lost or doomed, the sense of this slang noun.

clue.text: Make a statement about the left

parts.note: re means about, concerning
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Issue a press release about the political left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the left' sounds political, but it is port, the left side of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To give an account of events officially is a synonym for making a statement.

clue.text: Prince brought up to be commended

parts.note: a child brought up is raised

explanation.surface: A prince was raised to be admired.
explanation.definitionFit: Praised and commended both mean spoken of with approval.

clue.text: By the side of one left on a bit of ground

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: a bit of the word ground is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone stands beside a solitary person left on a patch of land.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk beside a river is to walk on its bank, so 'beside' is a synonym.

clue.text: Pulled together and strained

definitions.meaning: ... together, as curtains are pulled closed
a strained, tired face looks haggard

explanation.definitionFit: Curtains are closed by pulling; a tired, haggard face is described with the same past participle.

clue.text: Pedal gin

definitions.meaning: a serrated cycling pedal shaped like a vermin snare
a gin is a snare or trap for catching animals

explanation.definitionFit: A cycling pedal with toothed metal plates is named for a vermin snare, and a gin is such a snare.

clue.text: Stock made from oriental and onions

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Stock made from oriental and onions': TALON runs over orienTAL ONions only if the word 'and' is skipped, so no hidden run prints it; scan and search gave no other wording
annotationWithheld.clue: Stock made from oriental and onions

clue.text: Detest sailor getting order in a note

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
OM is the Order of Merit
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A sailor hates being given a command in a written note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' sounds like a command, but it is the Order of Merit, a British honour, OM.
explanation.definitionFit: Detest and loathe are synonyms.

clue.text: Type of monkey taking part in jungle murder

indicators.note: taking part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A monkey is involved in a killing in the jungle.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly, lemurs are primates but not monkeys.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemurs are Madagascan primates, loosely called monkeys.

clue.text: The arrogance of a bridge player with good cards

definitions.text: of a bridge player with good cards
definitions.meaning: read literally, holding a hand full of high cards

explanation.definitionFit: Overbearing behaviour is described by this word; read literally it means having a hand of top-ranking cards.
